title: Close the remaining local viewer mockup parity gaps

needs: The previous viewer parity pass made the page usable but did not lock down all visible surfaces from the reviewed mockup.
Operators must see the same major interaction areas as the mockup: command menus, a real Runbooks workspace, first-run splash guidance and the comparison split surface.
The browser smoke test must assert those surfaces directly so future parity claims fail when a major mockup block is missing.
context: The existing viewer remains a local, read-only HTML/CSS/JavaScript page over generated report data.
The reviewed mockup is the source of truth for the required menu, runbook, splash and compare structures.
This is a follow-up to the closed viewer parity request; the gap is specification coverage, not engine behavior.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The top bar exposes mockup-style command menus with grouped rows, separators, shortcuts or hints, and selectable CLI text; the menus never execute commands, fetch data or write files.

AC2: Selecting Runbooks replaces the central review area with a primary runbook coverage surface matching the mockup structure; rows show title, purpose, status and applied-operation chips, with unapplied runbooks visible.

AC3: Start opens the reviewed first-run splash surface with template command cards, recent-chain empty state, environment or doctor checks, fix commands and close or primary actions; no panel is blank.
AC4: Compare uses the mockup split layout with visible handle, before/after labels and metadata while preserving pointer drag and keyboard adjustment through a native control.

AC5: A real-browser smoke check opens the fixture page, exercises command menus, Runbooks, splash and Compare, and fails when required mockup selectors or states are absent; screenshots remain outside the repository.
AC6: The viewer keeps its safety boundary: no build step, no server, no engine execution, no privileged browser API, escaped report data and updated i18n strings for all new visible labels.

product.title: Strict local viewer mockup parity closure
product.overview: Tightens the viewer parity scope after the first pass by requiring the specific reviewed mockup surfaces that remain visibly different from the current implementation.
goals: Make menus, Runbooks, splash and Compare match the reviewed mockup at the structural interaction level.
Keep the viewer read-only and local while making command guidance discoverable.
Add browser smoke coverage that catches missing top-level mockup surfaces.
non_goals: Pixel-perfect rendering for every color, font metric or platform scrollbar.
A browser execution bridge, local daemon, job queue or engine control surface.
A framework, bundler, new dependency or hosted UI.
Geometry editing, report schema changes or operation behavior changes.

backlog_items.title: Replace minimal menus with the reviewed command menu surface
problem: The current viewer uses minimal native details menus and only a few command rows.
The mockup expects richer grouped command menus with shortcuts, separators and command-style rows.
scope_in: Reuse the existing static top bar and CSS.
Render grouped command rows, separators, shortcuts or hints and selectable CLI text.
Keep all menu actions informational or navigational inside the page.
scope_out: Clipboard permissions, shell execution, fetch calls or any write path.
Adding a menu framework or shared command registry before more than this viewer needs it.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Opening each menu shows grouped rows with visible shortcuts or hints and selectable CLI text.
AC2: Menu rows do not call fetch, spawn a process, mutate report files or require a server.
AC3: New visible menu labels are present in the i18n catalogue.

backlog_items.title: Build Runbooks as a primary workspace instead of an outliner-only list
problem: Runbooks currently appear mainly as outliner entries and detail-panel metadata.
The mockup shows a dedicated Runbooks screen with coverage rows and applied-operation relationships.
scope_in: Switching to Runbooks replaces the central review area with a runbook coverage body.
Rows show title, purpose, status and applied-operation chips using existing report and runbook data.
Unapplied or unavailable runbooks have explicit visible states.
scope_out: Executing runbook commands from the browser.
Persisted workflow state, external document fetching or schema changes.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The Runbooks workspace has a central list or table with one row per available runbook.
AC2: Applied operation chips are visible and selecting them focuses the linked report when data exists.
AC3: Unapplied runbooks remain visible with an explicit unapplied state instead of disappearing.

backlog_items.title: Restore the reviewed first-run splash and Compare split layout
problem: The current Start flow is a simpler panel rather than the reviewed splash surface.
The comparison image editor works but does not fully match the mockup split layout and metadata treatment.
scope_in: Start opens a splash-style surface with template command cards, recent-chain empty state, checks and fix commands.
Compare uses a split body with handle, labels, metadata and the existing native range interaction.
No-report and no-comparison states are explicit.
scope_out: Pixel-perfect screenshots as committed golden files.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The Start control opens and closes a splash surface with no blank columns or panels.
AC2: The splash lists starter template commands, recent-chain absence and environment or doctor state with fix guidance.
AC3: The Compare surface exposes before/after labels, a visible handle and a native control that remains draggable and keyboard-adjustable.

backlog_items.title: Make browser smoke fail on missing mockup surfaces
problem: The current smoke coverage can pass while major mockup surfaces are absent.
Screenshots help manual review, but the automated check must assert the required states directly.
scope_in: Exercise menu opening, Runbooks workspace, Start splash and Compare wipe in the existing Chrome smoke path.
Assert stable selectors or visible state for each required surface.
Write screenshots only to a temporary path outside the repository.
scope_out: New browser test dependencies when the existing smoke path is enough.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: One smoke command fails if menus, Runbooks, splash or Compare are missing.
AC2: The smoke changes the comparison wipe value and verifies the visible state changed.
AC3: No smoke screenshot or generated browser artifact is tracked by Git.

orchestration_task.title: Deliver remaining viewer mockup parity gaps
plan: Diff the mockup selectors against the current viewer and keep the required surface checklist in the task notes.
Implement command menus with the existing static page patterns.
Implement the Runbooks workspace as the primary center surface for that tab.
Implement the splash surface and Compare split layout without adding dependencies.
Extend the browser smoke to assert menus, Runbooks, splash and Compare.
Run make check, browser smoke and Logics validation before closeout.
